questions.knowledge_point: Solving Inequalities Requiring Division by a Positive Factor
questions.worked_solution:
Since ${4}^{x}+{x}^{2}$ is always positive, we can divide both sides of the inequality by this quantity. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{({4}^{x}+{x}^{2})(2x-3)}{{4}^{x}+{x}^{2}} & \ge \frac{0}{{4}^{x}+{x}^{2}} \\ 2x-3 & \ge 0 \\ 2x & \ge 3 \\ x & \ge \frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Since $x>2,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & >2 \\ {x}^{2} & >4 \\ {x}^{2}-3 & >1.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-3)$ is positive for all the values of $x$ that we are considering $(x>2).$ So, we can multiply both sides by $\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-3),$ and solve the resulting inequality as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5-2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-3)} & \ge 0 \\ (\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-3))\cdot \frac{5-2x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-3)} & \ge (\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-3))\cdot 0 \\ 5-2x & \ge 0 \\ -2x & \ge -5 \\ x & \le \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we had to flip the sign again of the inequality since we divided by a negative number ($-2$).

Therefore, the solution to the inequality will be the numbers that satisfy both $x>2$ and $x\le \frac{5}{2}.$ So, the solution to our inequality is $2<x\le \frac{5}{2}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving Inequalities Requiring Division by a Positive Factor
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the factor $|x-2|+3$ is always positive for all real numbers $x.$

Since $|x-2|+3$ is always positive, we can divide both sides of the inequality by this quantity. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(|x-2|+3)(4x-1)}{|x-2|+3} & \le \frac{0}{\,|x-2|+3\,} \\ 4x-1 & \le 0 \\ 4x & \le 1 \\ x & \le \,\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving Inequalities Requiring Multiplication or Division by a Negative Factor
questions.worked_solution:
Since $-4{x}^{2}-1$ is always negative, we can divide both sides of the inequality by this quantity, but we have to remember to flip the sign of the inequality. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-4{x}^{2}-1)(3x-2) & <0 \\ \frac{(-4{x}^{2}-1)(3x-2)}{-4{x}^{2}-1} & >\frac{0}{-4{x}^{2}-1} \\ 3x-2 & >0 \\ x & >\,\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

provenance.kp_title: Solving Inequalities Requiring Multiplication or Division by a Negative Factor

questions.worked_solution:
Since $x<8,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & <8 \\ x+1 & <9 \\ \sqrt{x+1} & <3 \\ \sqrt{x+1}-3 & <0.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $\sqrt{x+1}-3$ is negative for all the values of $x$ that we are considering $(x<8).$ So, we can divide both sides by $\sqrt{x+1}-3,$ provided that we flip the sign of the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\sqrt{x+1}-3)(x-2) & \le 0 \\ \frac{(\sqrt{x+1}-3)(x-2)}{\sqrt{x+1}-3} & \ge \frac{0}{\sqrt{x+1}-3} \\ x-2 & \ge 0 \\ x & \ge 2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the inequality will be the numbers that satisfy both $x\ge 2$ and $x<8.$ So, the solution to our inequality is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\le x<8\end{aligned}
$$
